ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Gibraltar Sanctions List, United Kingdom HM Treasury financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and Interpol notices. Enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons, their families, and close associates in accordance with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. Customer due diligence records must be refreshed at least annually and upon any material change of ownership or control. Sanctions screening must be completed before incorporation and prior to opening any payment rail or bank account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (electronic filing portal operated by the Registrar of Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the statutory language for all corporate filings. Names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet. A corporate identifier such as 'Limited' or 'Ltd' is required. Non-English names must include an English transliteration acceptable to the Registrar. In the case of a foreign company registered in Gibraltar, the endonym must be transliterated exactly where it uses non-Latin script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended at the Registrar’s discretion upon written application before the expiry of the 30-day window and payment of the applicable extension fee. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal in writing to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, attaching the original reservation receipt, the rejection letter, and any evidence of third-party clearance for sensitive tokens. For names containing sensitive tokens, the applicant must first obtain ministerial approval from the Competent Authority. The final remedy is an application for judicial review in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the registered-office address in Gibraltar when provided by a licensed corporate service provider, but it cannot constitute the commercial substance of the business. The ghost-kitchen and virtual-brand operation must maintain a substantive physical food-preparation facility registered with the Gibraltar Environmental Health Department. The registered office may serve only as the legal address and correspondence point.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk. Approximately 35% probability of an unannounced Financial Services Commission inspection in the first year after incorporation, plus mandatory pre-operational food-safety inspection and recurring unannounced environmental health inspections of the physical kitchen facility. The inspection likelihood increases to 55% where the company relies on virtual-office arrangements without demonstrating independent commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, ss. 1–24 (registration and incorporation), ss. 48–65 (share capital and shares), ss. 200–215 (directors); Companies (Exemptions from the Word 'Limited') Regulations; Income Tax (Exempt Companies) Regulations 2010
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Financial Services Commission, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Incorporation Application together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; minimum initial issue is one ordinary share, which may be nil-paid. Exempted company status does not require an escrow deposit, but if share capital exceeds GBP 1,000 the FSC may require confirmation of bank placement; no escrow mandate for an exempted operating/sheltered company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company is incorporated as a Bermuda Exempted Company under the Gibraltar Companies Act, and that the registered office be the address stated in the application. RESOLVED, that the subscriber has subscribed for one ordinary share, ratifying the allotment and approving all registers. RESOLVED, that the first directors and company secretary named in the application are appointed and their consents accepted. RESOLVED, that the directors are authorised to file incorporation documents, pay fees, open bank and merchant accounts, and execute contracts for the ghost kitchen. RESOLVED, that all required industrial and hygiene licences be submitted and this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar e-Portal (Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application confirming the entity name 'BM Exempted Co.' or a variant; the Registrar will run a conflict and prohibited-word check. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 28 days pending incorporation; obtain the written Name Approval Certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, file a fresh application with an alternative name or submit a letter of consent from the prior rights holder to overcome the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar notary public and licensed corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association with exempted-company clauses, share capital statement, initial directors, and company secretary details. Have the subscriber execute the documents before a Gibraltar notary; the notary will attest statutory declarations of compliance.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director forms
Consent to act as company secretary form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a correctness query, amend the affected schedule, reprint the clean execution set, and resubmit for notarization within the same working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (online filing window through a licensed agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the full incorporation pack via the Registrar's e-filing platform, including the executed constitutional documents, Form 1, and notarised declarations. Pay the official filing fee of USD 350 equivalent to the Registrar's escrow account; the agent will remit and upload proof of payment.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, respond with a written clarification and corrected pages within 21 days; where the query relates to fees, pay the required deficiency and resubmit the proof of payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Incorporation and Exempt Status Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies; Tax Office within the Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Simultaneously file the application for tax-exempted status under the Income Tax (Exempt Companies) Regulations; upon approval the Tax Office issues the Exempted Company Tax Certificate.
required_dossiers: Form for exempted company tax status
Declaration that the company will not trade with Gibraltar residents
Copy of the approved Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If exempt status is not appended automatically, apply for rectification using Form 3 or file an amended application with the Tax Office; any delayed certificate is backdated to the date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Company Secretary Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (registered office provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formally adopt the Gibraltar registered office address and appoint the qualified company secretary. File the corresponding notice of change or appointment via Form 7 and update the public register with the registered office address and officer details.
required_dossiers: Lease or service agreement for the Gibraltar registered office
Consent of company secretary to act
By-laws or board minute adopting the office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the filing for incomplete director physical address, collect certified proof of residential address and file a corrected Form 7 within the permitted cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Board Governance Adoption and Bank/Merchant Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar board of directors; Financial Services Commission (banking introduction)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the statutory first board meeting, adopt the first board resolution, and ratify share issuance, officer appointments, and commercial authorisations. Prepare the corporate residency file and introduction letter for opening bank/EMI accounts and payment merchant rails.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Certificate of Incorporation and Tax Exempt Certificate
Bank account introduction letter from the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or EMI requests additional source-of-funds evidence, obtain from the registered agent a certified copy of the incorporation record and provide personal bank statements of the subscriber covering the initial capital remittance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Environmental Protection Agency (MEPA – Ministry of Environment and Public Health)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Screening) – Environmental Impact Assessment registration required; full EIA report not required for low-risk kitchen preparation, but an abbreviated environmental statement is mandatory
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits: BOD5 ≤ 40 mg/L; suspended solids ≤ 60 mg/L; fats, oils and grease (FOG) ≤ 50 mg/L; pH 6.0–9.0; VOC grease-extraction exhaust stack ≤ 75 mg/Nm3; cooking-oil waste disposal must be performed by a licensed waste carrier with recorded manifest

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service fire safety certificate under BS 9999 or approved equivalence; structural load report from the Gibraltar Building Authority confirming floor-load capacity; occupational health clearance from the Gibraltar Health and Safety Inspectorate covering staff hygiene facilities, ventilation, and food-contact safety

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (P.O. Box 452, 17 Lonsdale Street, Gibraltar); HM Government of Gibraltar e-filing portal: https://incometax.gov.gi
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity (e.g., a Bermuda Exempted Company) that acquires a Gibraltar permanent establishment or has assessable Gibraltar-source income must first apply for a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN). The application is made to the Income Tax Office on Form C (Company Registration) and must include: a certified copy of the foreign certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents; a board resolution authorising the registration; a power of attorney in favour of the Gibraltar resident agent (if required); a statement of the principal place of effective management; and supporting evidence that the activity creates a chargeable presence. The ITO reviews the application and issues a TIN within ten business days. The company then becomes obliged to file annual tax returns (Form C) under the Income Tax Act 2010 and to appoint a tax representative if it is not tax-resident but carries on a trade in Gibraltar. If the entity has no chargeable nexus, it is not required to register, but may voluntarily apply for a TIN for administrative purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Bermuda Exempted Company is statutorily exempt from Bermudian income tax until 2035 under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, and that exemption follows the entity in its home jurisdiction. For Gibraltar tax purposes, the entity may deliver a non-residence declaration (Form NR) to the Income Tax Office to establish that its central management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar, thereby restricting Gibraltar tax liability to income sourced from a taxable permanent establishment. Gibraltar does not operate an equivalent to the U.S. 'check-the-box' classification regime; however, if the entity is owned by U.S. persons, a U.S. federal check-the-box election (Form 8832) may be made to treat the entity as a transparent (disregarded or partnership) entity, and such election may indirectly affect U.S. worldwide taxation but does not alter Gibraltar entity classification. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Gibraltar Taxation (Hybrid and Mismatch) Act 2021 may require a protective election where the entity is treated as taxable in a foreign jurisdiction and such treatment results in a deduction/no-inclusion mismatch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No general VAT/GST in Gibraltar; limited customs and excise duties apply on importation
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A – Gibraltar has no domestic value-added tax, goods and services tax, or sales and use tax, so no economic turnover threshold triggers indirect tax registration in Gibraltar. Where the ghost kitchen platform services are provided directly to final consumers in the United Kingdom through electronic platforms (e.g., UberEats, DoorDash), the entity may be required to register for UK VAT if UK taxable turnover exceeds the mandatory threshold of GBP 90,000 in any 12-month period; for non-established taxable persons, no threshold applies and registration is immediate. The relevant threshold is therefore not in Gibraltar currency (GIP) but in British pounds sterling when UK supplies are made.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not mandate electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API interoperability for supplier invoices. A conventional paper or PDF invoice is sufficient for tax audit purposes. For imports into Gibraltar, a customs declaration must be submitted electronically through the approved Gibraltar Customs EDI system, but without transactional pre-approval. For UK VAT obligations, HMRC’s Making Tax Digital regime requires digital record-keeping and submission of VAT returns via HMRC-approved API software; invoices may be issued electronically but are not subject to live clearance or government stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: As Gibraltar has no VAT or GST, all exports of tangible goods from Gibraltar to any destination outside Gibraltar are automatically outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect taxation; they attract no Gibraltar exit duty and are therefore effectively zero-rated. To substantiate export treatment for customs and foreign tax purposes, the exporter must demonstrate that (a) the goods physically departed from Gibraltar and were delivered to a customer located outside Gibraltar; (b) legal title and risk of loss passed to that overseas customer; and (c) any invoiced amount was paid in a freely convertible currency or by an approved compensating payment. With respect to offshore services (including ghost kitchen franchise know-how, brand licensing, and central administrative services supplied from Gibraltar), the place of supply is determined under the Income Tax Act and not under a VAT framework; no Gibraltar export tax is levied, and the entity is not required to charge any export VAT. For goods that, via the online marketplace, enter the UK, zero-rating for UK VAT is available only if the goods meet the UK zero-rated export criteria, which include proof of removal from the UK within 30 days of supply and retention of a valid customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document or electronic equivalent)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / other transport evidence showing departure from Gibraltar
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of payment in foreign currency within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims are aggressively scrutinised. Under the Gibraltar Customs and Excise Duties Ordinance, deliberate false documentation in support of an export claim is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of up to seven years and an unlimited fine. Civil consequences include recovery of any unpaid duty or tax (if a foreign VAT applies), interest at the statutory rate, and additional penalties of up to 200% of the total amount evaded. For UK VAT, where a Gibraltar-based entity improperly claims zero-rating on goods supplied into the UK, HMRC may issue a retrospective assessment extending back to the statutory limit of 20 years in cases of deliberate or concealed error; a penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded may be imposed, plus a detailed disclosure may be required under the UK Finance Act 2021. The Australian-style 'clawback' concept is transposed by the recovery provisions in the Gibraltar Taxation (International and Other Provisions) Act 2020, which disapplies treaty or exemption benefits where the principal purpose is to achieve a tax advantage, thereby enabling retrospective reclassification of exports and full recovery of underpaid indirect tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Government of Gibraltar, acting under the Currency Notes Act 1934, issues the Gibraltar Pound (GIP) at a statutory 1:1 peg to GBP, with the Bank of England as the ultimate monetary backstop. The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) licenses and supervises all credit institutions and payment services. No standalone central-bank exchange-control administration exists within Gibraltar; HM Treasury and the Bank of England apply the UK monetary framework, and the GFSC oversees the practical execution for all GIP-denominated clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar operates a fully convertible current and capital account. GIP is freely exchangeable into GBP at par without any fiscal charge, and USD/EUR accounts are permitted without restriction for corporate treasury. Profit remittance is free of all Gibraltar withholding taxes—no dividend, interest, or royalty WHT—and the Bermuda Exempted Company status is classified as non-resident for Bermuda Exchange Control Act purposes, permitting unfettered capital movement between shareholders, the company, and its Gibraltar operating accounts without Bermuda Monetary Authority approval. No capital-account authorization or profit-repatriation permit is required in either jurisdiction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Neither Gibraltar nor the United Kingdom imposes any mandatory surrender percentage, conversion timeline, or holding-period requirement for export or platform proceeds. DoorDash/UberEats USD receivables may be held indefinitely in USD-denominated Gibraltarian accounts, freely converted at any market rate, or routed via UK/EEA clearing without central-bank pre-authorization. Bermuda's Exchange Control regulations likewise exempt a non-resident Exempted Company from any surrender obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for inbound aggregation; Medium-Low as a full treasury substitute. A Bermuda Exempted Company may lawfully use UK FCA-licensed E-Money Institutions (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payoneer) and US-based payment gateways (Airwallex, Stripe Treasury) to collect DoorDash/UberEats USD payouts and convert to GBP/EUR. Legal constraint: the EEA financial-services passport does not extend to Gibraltar, so a UK EMI cannot establish a licensed branch within Gibraltar; it may, however, service the corporate client without a Gibraltar EMI licence. If a GFSC-regulated local EMI is preferred, a full Electronic Money licence will be required under the Financial Services Ordinance 2015, which is only practical for established settlement volumes. Recommended architecture: an EMI for global payment aggregation, layered over a Tier-1 Gibraltar bank for statutory clearing and supplier settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted for lower-risk structures. The three principal Gibraltar clearing banks (GIBank, Trusted Novus, Jyske) accept scheduled video-KYC interviews for the beneficial owner and one signatory director, provided the company delivers a notarised board resolution, a certified apostilled copy of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing, an incumbency certificate, passport copies, and a live compliance call confirming the ghost-kitchen commercial purpose. Physical attendance is not mandatory; however, if enhanced due diligence is triggered by non-EEA UBOs or high USD aggregation volume, the bank may require one countersigning local licensed TCSP director to attend the compliance meeting in person. Each GIBank account mandate must identify the UBO register and the approved signatory matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-tax Bermuda 'Exempted' classification combined with Gibraltar management and control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Registrar Certificate of Exempted Status; Bermuda Economic Substance Act filing (BES-G form); Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax tax-residency ruling or a legal opinion on place of effective management; audited management accounts evidencing substance (kitchen lease, payroll register, supplier contracts); signed entity-risk questionnaire confirming the tax-neutral flow-through model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity payment aggregator inflows with no customer invoices to individual diners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Merchant Agreements with DoorDash and UberEats; processor settlement statements for at least three months; aggregated gross-sales reports for the relevant platform; flow-of-funds chart showing that no third-party sub-payment or 'processing-for-others' activity occurs; a compliance undertaking to provide quarterly platform payout reconciliations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners resident outside the UK/EEA and all settlement denominated in USD
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PSC-style register of persons with significant control; notarised and apostilled passport copies of every UBO owning 25% or more; banker's financial reference for each UBO; source-of-wealth statement; OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening results for all directors and UBOs; corporate LEI code issued to the Bermuda entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial low equity base versus rapid scaling projections for multi-brand kitchen capacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising the initial capital injection; SWIFT MT103 credit advices evidencing the funds landing; 12-month cash-flow forecast and unit economics model; committed kitchen sub-leases and supplier framework agreements; letter from the Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider confirming statutory register maintenance and economic-substance reporting calendars.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda registered office only, with no physical operational evidence in Gibraltar
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: If intended to remain non-Gibraltar resident: signed declaration confirming that management decisions are taken offshore and a substance dossier from the actual jurisdiction; if a Gibraltar permanent establishment is accepted: lease or sub-lease agreement for the kitchen premises, Gibraltar FPS payroll registration as an employer, utility and rates invoices, and a director's availability plan for any proposed inspection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's or UBO's bank to the entity's GIBank account. Populate Field 57A with the beneficiary bank's BIC, Field 59 with the company name and account number, and Field 70 with 'EQUITY INJECTION PER BOARD RESOLUTION [DD-MMM-YYYY]'. Field 33B must show the currency and amount, and the LEI should be appended in Field 72. The receiving bank will require the board resolution, the shareholder approval letter, CRS/FATCA self-certification, and a source-of-funds statement. For intercompany loans exceeding GBP 85,000, attach the executed loan agreement and the Bermuda BMA negative-consent confirmation for non-resident Exempted Companies; no Gibraltar exchange-control notification applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) UK Faster Payments Service (FPS) for on-island and UK supplier settlements in GBP; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-UK vendor payments (food costs, packaging, equipment); (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR-denominated payouts to EU suppliers; (4) CHAPS for same-day high-value GBP disbursements covering rent and payroll. Commercial Letters of Credit are not required for standard operating disbursements; a revocable or revolving MT700 LC should be reserved exclusively for large frozen-food or equipment imports from non-EU counterparties. DoorDash/UberEats platform commissions are debited directly from each payout statement, requiring no additional clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/GBP and EUR/GBP) executed under an ISDA/EMTA master agreement with a Gibraltar-licensed bank
FX swaps combining spot and forward legs, used to net USD payout receipts against GBP operational obligations
Cross-currency swaps (GBP/USD) aligning long-term intercompany loans or term-debt service requirements
Plain-vanilla FX options (USD call/GBP put) protecting platform revenue volumes against adverse sterling moves
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible only for exotic-currency speculative exposure; not necessary for USD/GBP or EUR/GBP, which are fully deliverable in Gibraltar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR01) under Companies Act 2014
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of GBP 250; continued non-compliance triggers a notice of proposed strike-off and subsequent dissolution under the Companies Act 2014.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than 10 months after the end of the accounting reference period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors liable to civil penalty of up to GBP 5,000 and potential disqualification; registry strike-off proceedings commence after two consecutive missed filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company income tax self-assessment return (Form IT01)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 September following the tax year for calendar-year accounting periods; otherwise nine months after period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 5% of tax due initially, escalating to 20% after six months; interest and collection enforcement apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies House – Registrar of Companies (UBO Section)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after each anniversary of incorporation; changes filed within 14 days of any shareholding movement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and Level 5 offence on default; repeated failure results in company strike-off and suspension of a certificate of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food business operator / ghost kitchen annual licence renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Environmental Health and Licensing Department, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 1 January; renewal window opens 60 days prior
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate suspension of delivery-only kitchen operations; daily penalty of GBP 100 until a valid licence is produced.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full statutory audit is mandatorily required for any Gibraltar company not qualifying as small under the Companies Act 2014 (turnover over GBP 2 million, balance-sheet total over GBP 1 million, or more than 50 employees). The exempted-company structure applied here is additionally conditioned on annual audit irrespective of those thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted for Gibraltar; Companies Act 2014 requires financial statements to comply with IFRS / the Gibraltar equivalent and to be prepared in English.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of beneficial owners must be verified annually on the anniversary of incorporation and the verification filed with the Registrar of Companies UBO Section within 14 days; any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be reflected in the statutory registers and filed within 14 days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Bermuda Exempted Company classification: complete exemption from Bermuda taxation on foreign-source receipts; Gibraltar taxation at 10% applies solely to profits attributable to a permanent establishment in Gibraltar. No special incentive or tax holiday for delivery-only ghost kitchen operations; capital allowances and loss relief may lower the effective rate in start-up years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Company Tax Return (Form CT) filed electronically via the Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-Tax portal (https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the accounting period end; tax year of assessment is the calendar year in which the accounting period ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification - registered name, subsisting Bermuda registration number and Gibraltar tax reference (when appointed).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Bermuda Exempted Company's full legal name exactly as on the certificate of incorporation; do not omit the word 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show the period covered by the Gibraltar branch accounts; it may differ from Bermuda's exemption certificate year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar-source trading turnover (gross receipts from UberEats, DoorDash and other delivery platform payouts).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to the Gibraltar kitchen; exclude any amount channelled through the Bermuda entity without local substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenditure - ingredient procurement, kitchen rental, salaries, platform fees, leased kitchen overheads, and virtual brand royalty payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenditure incurred for the Gibraltar permanent establishment; related-party expenditure must separately satisfy transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable profit (or loss) before reliefs - reconciled to the statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Bermudan exempt company has a PE, the adjusted profit must be determined at arm's length from the associated foreign entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief, capital allowances, and donations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim trading loss carryforward limited to 5 years; capital allowances on kitchen fixtures and equipment are available if incurred by the Gibraltar branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax due or payable, after credit for any withholding or advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where no DTA claim is made, tax is payable at 10% of Box 5 amount; unpaid balances incur interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of £250; an automatic surcharge of £125 for returns outstanding up to three months; an additional daily penalty of £20 per day (capped at £1,000) thereafter; late payment interest accrues at 8% per annum and the total sanction may be increased to 100% of the tax where there is neglect or deliberate concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For the zero-rate domestic dividend withholding tax, no treaty relief application is required in Gibraltar. Where a payer in a treaty state imposes withholding tax on dividend distributions from the Bermuda Exempted Company, a Gibraltar tax residency certificate (TRC) is needed. Apply to the Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax for a TRC, evidencing central management and control in Gibraltar; attach audited financial statements, the Form CT return, and a certificate of tax residency. The TRC is submitted to the foreign payer within 30 days before the dividend payment; if the foreign payer already withheld tax, a refund claim must be filed with the source state's tax authority within the relevant statute of limitations, citing the specific treaty article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: no Gibraltar withholding tax on royalties or interest paid to non-residents. Treaty (UK-Gibraltar DTA typically applies): royalties may be charged at 0% and interest at 0% for banks and governmental bodies, otherwise reduced to 10% where the Gibraltar-resident beneficial owner provides a TRC. A mere Bermuda Exempted Company without Gibraltar CMC will not ordinarily be eligible for the treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Gibraltar Economic Substance (Companies) Act 2018 and the OECD Substance requirements apply. Any Bermuda Exempted Company operating a ghost kitchen through a Gibraltar PE must show core income-generating activity locally: the kitchen lease, the virtual brand management, delivery coordination, procurement decisions, and staff payroll must all be directed and staffed from Gibraltar. Failure to satisfy substance will trigger reclassification of the PE as a tax-resident shell and disqualify treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming tax-exempt status under the Bermuda certificate while operating a Gibraltar PE without filing Form CT or paying 10% Gibraltar tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revenue assessment on all Gibraltar-source profit; negligence/deliberate penalty up to 100% of the tax; interest at 8% per annum; court fine not exceeding £250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly abused the exemption may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax; travel bans are imposed in serious cases; imprisonment up to two years for fraudulent evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No physical kitchen, employees, or operational substance in Gibraltar while booking all UberEats/DoorDash income offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Action by the Gibraltar Commissioner: penalty of £1,500 under the Economic Substance Act; a further £5,000 for failure to file the substance return; and dissolvement or strike-off of the entity if correction notices are ignored.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be subject to disqualification orders and civil fines; the court may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for all unpaid tax and statutory payroll contributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register return; use of bearer shares or undocumented nominee shareholders to shield the virtual brand ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to GIP 100,000 per offence; confiscation orders; disqualification of professional advisers; bank account freezing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability for money laundering if the shell is used to move proceeds from delivery operations; prison terms of up to five years and travel restrictions apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties or service fees to the Bermuda exempted parent so that the Gibraltar kitchen PE records a taxable loss.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profit to an arm's length amount at 10%; interest at 8% per annum; transfer pricing penalty of GIP 2,000 or up to 25% of the shortfall disclosed in a scheme report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable in tort for assisting in a tax rule misrepresentation; civil restitution orders are issued in the Gibraltar courts; extradition to the UK may be sought for deliberate underdeclaration.
